continuity_scope: Capcom Town’s current English Home Console Breath of Fire witness, whose game details are expressly based on the English version; Nintendo’s English UK Virtual Console listing identifies the release as the US version on Wii U (27 November 2014) and New Nintendo 3DS (6 October 2016). This narrow pass does not equate those archives with the 1993 original, Japanese release, ports, later patches, or any other numbered Breath of Fire game.
work_or_witnesses: Capcom Town, Breath of Fire, Home Console English classic game page
Nintendo UK, Breath of Fire Virtual Console product page
coverage_rule: Every individually named dramatic character in the selected Capcom Town English narrative: Ryu only. The page identifies an unnamed sister, unnamed Light/Dark Dragon groups, and seven unnamed companions; no non-Ryu name is supplied, so no other character node is made. Clans, dragons, animal powers, transformations, companions, places, mechanics, and enemies remain terms/dimensions.
omissions: Ryu’s unnamed sister, all seven unnamed companions, all unlisted antagonist and supporting characters, clans, dragons, animals, items, places, systems, and player party states.

Breath of Fire II–VI, all port/Virtual Console/Capcom Town service behavior beyond stated archival boundaries, Japanese/other localizations, cameos, crossovers, fan wikis, Wikipedia, walkthroughs, and community databases.
uncertainties: The Capcom Town page is a very short official series/game synopsis rather than a manual or complete cast profile list; pass-complete applies only to its single named figure.

Capcom Town says details are based on the English version but does not state an original platform/release date; Nintendo’s older Virtual Console listing is used only for English US-version archival clarification.
Ryu’s sister and companions are narratively present but unnamed in this witness, so no relationship endpoints or claimed party roster are possible.
evidence_basis: Capcom first-party English classic-game description, supplemented by Nintendo’s first-party English Virtual Console archive for version/localization boundary. No fan source is used as canonical evidence.
